paper.pageLocations: HTML sections and figure captions verified; PDF pagination for individual passages not verified.

population.maleData: The parent cohort included boys, but this paper’s fitted hormone trajectories concern girls only.

assay.loq: not separately supplied in main article
assay.valuesBelowDetection: Research data represented below-LOD/LOQ values at half the respective threshold; this does not authorize substitution of patient results.

figure1.statistic: Age-dependent GAMLSS median and ±1/±2 SD curves
figure1.model: Box-Cox GAMLSS with smoothed age-dependent L, M, S. Treats the repeated measurements as a cross-sectional sample for this purpose.
figure1.yUnit: analyte-specific concentration; LH and FSH IU/L
figure1.clinicalRole: Source of quantitative age-specific median/reference distributions; existing educational patient marker uses this independently from display geometry.
figure1.verifiedVisualFinding: FSH median is almost horizontal; LH median declines early and has only a weak later bump. Current source-table curves resemble these black median curves.

figure3.statistic: Longitudinal population mean trajectory, normalized separately for each hormone
figure3.model: Maximum-likelihood linear mixed model; natural-spline fixed mean, Gaussian random spline coefficients with unrestricted covariance, independent Gaussian measurement noise. Spline degrees of freedom searched from 3 through 12 using AIC.
figure3.normalization: mean concentration at age / maximum of that hormone’s mean trajectory
figure3.yUnit: dimensionless, not IU/L; not normalized individually per infant; not normalized against adult/menopausal concentration
figure3.relativeAmplitudes: Approximate digitization retained in display-data.json: LH first peak 0.999759 and second 0.183082; FSH first 0.996168 and second 0.760254. These are dimensionless model mean ratios, not IU/L.
figure3.verifiedVisualFinding: Original image shows distinct first and second waves for both LH and FSH. These differ materially from the medians in Fig.1.
figure3.mainLimitation: No physical-unit maximum, fitted coefficients, selected degrees of freedom by hormone, or mean-trajectory numerical table found in this article or its two linked public supplements.
figure3.timingScope: Approximate population-level model peak timings reported for this cohort, not universal clinical days, individual peak predictions, or validated diagnostic thresholds.

supplements.scope: One DOCX: reference lines −2 SD, −1 SD, median, +1 SD, +2 SD and L,M,S for all seven hormones. These do not encode the separate longitudinal mean model.
One PDF of individual longitudinal observations and reference curves. LH/FSH axes are logarithmic. No raw numerical observations or mean-model coefficients.
supplements.absoluteMeanScale: Not supplied. Physical-unit axes belong to individual observed concentrations and GAMLSS reference curves. They do not provide the separate Figure3 longitudinal mean maxima or fixed-effect model.

availability.articleDeclaration: The article restricts some/all underlying data for confidentiality or licensing, with conditions available from the corresponding author on request.
searchScope: Both linked public Figshare supplements and current metadata
Web queries combining article DOI/title with code, GitHub, spline and data availability
availability.result: No numerical mean model or analysis code found in the inspected materials. This does not establish that authors have never shared additional data elsewhere.
availability.scatterReconstruction: Not attempted. No cohort mean was reconstructed by averaging/digitizing plotted individuals or by multiplying normalized Figure3 by GAMLSS median maxima.

provenance.statistic: population longitudinal mean from random-coefficient natural-spline model
provenance.normalization: Each hormone mean concentration divided by that hormone mean maximum. No absolute maximum was provided.
provenance.population: 98 healthy term infant girls, Copenhagen; 266 serum samples; earliest real sampling day5.
provenance.reconstruction: Colour-mask trace centre at each available image column; PCHIP fills only bounded dashed gaps. Sparse day anchors sampled from that trace. No concentrations in IU/L reconstructed.
provenance.clinicalReference: Does not alter numerical GAMLSS median, reference limits, assay qualification or patient results.
provenance.timingScope: Approximate shape and cohort-model timing, not universally exact physiologic ages.

calibration.digitizationUncertainty: Pixel position and curve width imply approximate relative values. These are not raw model predictions, confidence intervals or assay precision.

sourcePixelAgreement.residualMeaning: Residual to column colour centres, including line intersections/occlusion and antialiasing; not accuracy against unavailable original model. Sparse anchors intentionally avoid tracing every raster wiggle.

lh.terminalPolicy: Retain the gentle late behavior present in the source; do not characterize the small rise as a third physiologic wave. No invented terminal plateau. FSH presentation stops at day357, omitting only the final rounded dash cap (raw trace continues to357.294643).

sourcePixelAgreement.residualMeaning: Residual to column colour centres, including line intersections/occlusion and antialiasing; not accuracy against unavailable original model. Sparse anchors intentionally avoid tracing every raster wiggle.

fsh.terminalPolicy: Retain the gentle late behavior present in the source; do not characterize the small rise as a third physiologic wave. No invented terminal plateau. FSH presentation stops at day357, omitting only the final rounded dash cap (raw trace continues to357.294643).

lh.reason: visible axis endpoint within tick calibration precision

reproducibility.coordinateSystem: Original 3600 × 2622 image pixel coordinates. Linear tick calibration is retained in calibration.

colourMasks.lh: blue > red + 20, red > green + 20, red < 200, green < 120

reproducibility.trace: At available image columns x=300..3075 and y<2398, take median matching pixel y. Convert to day/value using calibration. Values within 0.003 of the published 0..1 axis were clipped for line-width/antialiasing residue.
reproducibility.interpolation: PCHIP fills only gaps between available trace columns. Sparse ages explicitly retained below; no fit to median/physical-unit data.
reproducibility.endpoints: FSH ends at day 357, omitting a rounded dash-cap residue to 357.294643. LH last readable point snaps to day 360 by less than the measured x-tick residual. No extension to birth/day 365.
reproducibility.uncertainty: Raster-derived approximate model means, not raw fitted predictions. Source-pixel residuals include occlusion and anti-aliasing; they are not confidence limits or assay uncertainty.

secondarySourceCorrection.implication: Use primaryverifiednumbers; this isolated maleerror doesnot invalidate verifiedfemalerows.

hCGInterpretation: 3% crossreactivity means assayresponse to hCG, not a fixed3% share ofevery measured LHvalue.
No simultaneous hCG concentrations or sample-specific corrections are reported. Do not subtract3% from LH or derive a numerical correction fromage alone.
ResidualhCG could bias especiallyearlyneonatal LH upward; originalRIA is not automaticallyinterchangeable withlaterImmulite orAutoDELFIA assays.
The paper remains evidence ofsource-specific neonatal gonadotropinpatterns. Crossreactivity doesnot byitself proveeverylaterLH elevation isartefact, nor establishan exact calibration betweenstudies.
FirstdaysLHmedian0.20 isnearLOD0.15. Do not pretend these numbers support fineresolution day-byday physiology.
clinicalConclusions: Lowearlyvalues followedbyhigherfemaleLH groups in thefirstmonth are real observations in thiscohort. A flatJi2–12monthLH line is incomplete as an illustration ofthefirstmonth.
FSH dominatesLH in allfemale groups; preserve thisrelationship onsharedIU/Laxis.
The reported twoFSH peaks are cross-sectional group features, not repeated twopeaks documented within eachinfant.
Smallagegroups, pulsatility andassay issues prohibit interpreting everydip orpeak as a compulsory developmental event.
The source beginsday1 andgroupsdays1–5. It doesnotprovide a birth/day0meanormedian or justify zero.
Numeric patientreferenceprofiles must remain independent of anyeducational interpolation.

primarySource.title: Gonadotropins and Sex Hormones in Healthy Chinese Infants
verification: Original PDF table screenshot, including decimal points and censor signs.
primarySource.snapshotType: Browser-tool text response containing the original publisher article. Not a downloaded PDF binary; direct HTTP returned403.

cohort.population: Healthy full-term Chinese infants, appropriate for gestational age; normal physical examination.
cohort.exactAgeBinBoundaries: Not specified. Do not invent bin boundaries or treat group labels as precise individual ages.
cohort.design: Age-group series; repeated sampling within the same infants is not established by the methods. Do not describe as a serial within-child trajectory.
exclusions: Cerebral trauma, kidney disease, congenital cardiopathy or malformations

assay.compatibility: Do not assume interchangeability with AutoDELFIA (Ljubicic2022) or later Siemens IMMULITE2000XPi merely because analytes/units overlap.

discrepancies: Methods prose calls bounds 95% confidence intervals. Preserve the table's stated percentile labels with this uncertainty; do not present them as confidence bands for a median.
Results prose reports female LH0.36 at2–3months, inconsistent with TableI (0.2 at2/3months;0.3 at4months). For extracted numbers use TableI.
General prose describes gonadotropins reaching juvenile levels by6months; femaleFSH table medians remain5.4–5.7IU/L at6–12months. Do not force femaleFSH to a nearzero male-like course.

comparisonStudyNotSpliced.kind: Public1989 doctoral thesis, chapter7.2 submitted manuscript preceding1990 publication, not asserted to be identical final published full text.
comparisonStudyNotSpliced.finalAbstractCrosscheck: 1990 publisher abstract independently agrees with55/75-year predictions andn680.
comparisonStudyNotSpliced.selection: Follow-up of a population survey; excludes17 women withE2>100pmol/L from697 complete datasets. This is not a repeatedly sampled within-person55→75 trajectory.
comparisonStudyNotSpliced.assayLHFSH: IRE-Medgenix radioimmunometric assays, distinct from AutoDELFIA.
comparisonStudyNotSpliced.statistic: Table3 univariate age-regression predicted values; not observed age-bin medians and not reference limits.
comparisonStudyNotSpliced.canReconstruct: A straight regression trend between those rounded model predictions is source-derived interpolation, not invented annual measurements. Do not infer unsupported endpoints outside this range.
comparisonStudyNotSpliced.cannotDo: No validated assay conversion to AutoDELFIA, no early adulthood or menopausal-transition curve, no90-year values, no individual percentile band. Do not splice at55 as if the jump reflects menopause or biology.

sourceDetails.title: The LH/FSH ratio is not a sex-dimorphic marker after infancy: data from 6417 healthy individuals and125 patients with Differences of Sex Development
sourceDetails.population: 3273 healthy females in pooled cohorts; adult20–<40 female group only17; cycles not standardized. AutoDELFIA, LOD0.05IU/L.
sourceDetails.statisticWarning: TableI group entries are not explicitly identified as mean versus median. Do not relabel as p50.
clinicalMeaning: Adult reproductive-age group LH5.63 andFSH4.44IU/L; postmenopausal age groups much higher. Broad age groups do not diagnose menopause status or exact transition age.
Cross-method/cohort stitching from Madsen female16years LH5.65/FSH5.83 to adult5.63/4.44 does not justify an abrupt biological fall at16–18.
Use a broad modest adult transition for illustration and retain original source numbers separately. Do not fit local trough/rebound through sparse age-group centers.
Menopause-related FSH increase supports much larger whole-life concentrations; must not determine zoom scale for childhood/puberty.

Population p50 and group maturation patterns are not a single woman’s menstrual trajectory.

cycle.title: Establishment of detailed reference values for luteinizing hormone, follicle stimulating hormone, estradiol, and progesterone during different phases of the menstrual cycle on the Abbott ARCHITECT analyzer
cycle.sourceVersion: Public author/laboratory-hosted PDF marked Article in press - uncorrected proof; published journal citation44(7):883–887; do not call this the final typeset version.

population.exclusions: No oral contraceptives or other medications
population.ovulation: All cycles included were ovulatory;3 transvaginalUS examinations atcycle days10/13 and1or2days postovulation assessed follicular/corpusluteum development.

methods.frequency: Daily during one cycle per volunteer
methods.alignment: Day0 is the day of each volunteer’s measured LH maximum. This aligns variable cycles; it is NOT universally day14 after menstruation and is not necessarily the exact instant of ovulation.

phaseTable.meaning: These are reported phase medians; NOT midpoint of a reference interval and NOT a measured concentration at phase-midpoint day.

cycle.uncertainty: Small20-woman cohort, daily counts8–20. Authors explicitly caution5th/95th percentiles whenn<19; median traces show this cohort, not universal diagnostic limits. Small day-to-day fluctuations of group medians must not be promoted to fixed biological events.
